recommendations.regimenLabel: Transfuse if symptomatic/severe + treat the deficiency
steps: Assess haemodynamic tolerance; transfuse for symptomatic/severe anaemia (restrictive threshold ~70 g/L, ~80 if cardiac).
Identify and treat the cause — iron/B12/folate deficiency, bleeding, haemolysis, marrow, chronic disease.
Iron deficiency: oral iron (IV if intolerant/malabsorption) and find the source (GI evaluation in at-risk).
Replace B12/folate as indicated (give B12 before folate to avoid subacute combined degeneration).
Reticulocyte count and blood film direct further work-up.

drugRefs.dose: 1 unit, then reassess (restrictive threshold ~70 g/L; ~80 g/L if cardiac)
drugRefs.freq: single-unit transfusion, reassess symptoms/Hb between units
drugRefs.why: Restores oxygen-carrying capacity in symptomatic or severe anaemia; single-unit, restrictive strategy avoids over-transfusion.

drugRefs.dose: 200 mg (≈65 mg elemental iron) once daily to twice daily
drugRefs.duration: continue ~3 months after Hb normalises to replenish stores
drugRefs.why: First-line correction of iron-deficiency anaemia; identify and treat the source of loss.

drugRefs.dose: 1 mg IM on alternate days initially, then 1 mg every 2–3 months
drugRefs.why: Corrects B12 deficiency; give before folate to avoid precipitating subacute combined degeneration of the cord.
Corrects folate-deficiency anaemia; ensure B12 is replete first.

recommendations.regimenLabel: IV iron when oral iron unsuitable

drugRefs.dose: dose per weight/Hb deficit (commonly up to 1000 mg per infusion)
drugRefs.freq: single/repeat infusions to replace calculated deficit
drugRefs.why: For oral-iron intolerance, malabsorption or need for rapid repletion.

decision.label: Transfuse if symptomatic; treat the underlying deficiency

confirm: Fatigue, dyspnoea, pallor, tachycardia with low haemoglobin; classify by MCV and look for blood loss/haemolysis.
